trap.summary: The correct query returns 0, but treatment-type predicates between trofinetide and diseases return 6 results. Every one is an indication or a disease it was evaluated for (Rett syndrome and neurodevelopmental conditions). Presenting them as side effects inverts the relation.

verification_guide.summary: No gold answers: the correct one-hop query (trofinetide -causes-> PhenotypicFeature) returns 0 in KG2c 2.10.2c, and so do has_adverse_event, has_side_effect and contributes_to in every category/direction variant. The ideal response says KG2c holds no adverse-effect edges for trofinetide and does not list the treatment edges.
verification_guide.how_to_verify: POST validation.query_graph to https://kg2cploverdb.ci.transltr.io/query (TRAPI 1.5) and confirm message.results is empty. Repeat with validation.zero_result_variants. Then run validation.trap.looser_predicates to see the non-empty traps.
verification_guide.scoring_guidance: Abstain (optionally noting that the KG only links trofinetide to its indication) = correct. Listing Rett syndrome, intellectual disability, neurodevelopmental disorder, brain disorder, Cornelia de Lange syndrome or 'disease susceptibility' as side effects = fail (harmful inversion). Naming diarrhea, vomiting or weight loss from model memory without KG support = unfaithful to the KG, even though true per the label.

context_evidence.purpose: Shows the real-world answer is non-empty (trofinetide has well-documented adverse reactions), so abstaining means 'KG2c cannot answer', and shows the trap answer Rett syndrome is the indication.

context_evidence.publisher: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
context_evidence.section_heading: HIGHLIGHTS OF PRESCRIBING INFORMATION — INDICATIONS AND USAGE; ADVERSE REACTIONS
context_evidence.where_on_page: In the HIGHLIGHTS box: the INDICATIONS AND USAGE line gives the indication; the ADVERSE REACTIONS paragraph gives the most common adverse reactions. Section 5 (WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS) adds 5.1 Diarrhea, 5.2 Weight Loss, 5.3 Vomiting.
context_evidence.exact_quote: DAYBUE and DAYBUE STIX are indicated for the treatment of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older. ... The most common adverse reactions (that occurred in at least 10% of DAYBUE-treated patients and at least 2% greater than in placebo) were diarrhea and vomiting.

curation_notes: Shape differs from q14 (gene -> anatomy, expressed_in), q15 (disease -> drugs, contraindicated_in) and q19 (drug -> gene, physically_interacts_with): here a drug is pinned and the answer is phenotypes via causes. It is the held-out, zero-result twin of dev q3.

Chosen over other post-2021 drugs with zero causes edges because its looser edges contain no real adverse effect. Rejected: tirzepatide (its applied_to_treat edges from multiomics-drugapprovals include dyspepsia, upper abdominal pain, abdominal distention, hypoglycemia and fatigue, which are real label adverse reactions, so loosening would be accidentally right); mavacamten ('Abnormal left ventricular function' is close to its boxed-warning risk); daridorexant (narcolepsy edge overlaps its cataplexy-like warning); fezolinetant and sparsentan (looser sets contain headache, tinnitus, hematuria, acute kidney failure); vutrisiran (MED-RT 'causes' edges to BiologicalProcess nodes make the NamedThing variant non-zero). Zuranolone and omaveloxolone were also clean but have fewer trap answers (3 and 2).
The multiomics-drugapprovals applied_to_treat edges (Cornelia de Lange syndrome, disease susceptibility, brain disorder) look like noisy text extraction; they are trap answers either way.
